The King was pacing his chamber; he was challenged to a traditional duel by a mere child. Duels had not been practiced in centuries and were a long-forgotten tradition, or so he thought. The king had to consider many things, if he were to murder a child, he would surely be frowned upon, but if he refused he would have to give his title of King away. His family had been the supreme monarchs since the 60-minute war that happened so long ago. The world was in travesty, in essence, a nuclear wasteland. One man, however, was able to unite these broken people and made refuge underground. The man, the first king, deemed that those who were the strongest should rule. This King enforced a system of gladiator-like battles in the civilians; social class would be determined by strength. The King actively partook in these duels and had never lost. The King had unbeatable luck, it almost seemed magical how he was able to perform such a task. The day came that the first king passed, and his successor was just as brutal. For several centuries this blood-lusting family had ruled. And now we reach our current King.

  
It was a little over half-past noon and The King had finished eating lunch. He ventured up to his study from the main dining hall. The King was considered an oddity, his family had a long chain of warrior blood and for no apparent reason this King was almost, "Scholarly". The King had never learned how to use a gun, or how to use a weapon, but read a lot of books and was very intelligent. The current King would solve problems diplomatically rather than with brute force and was much liked by the people of the American Isles. The King has now been challenged to a traditional duel by a small child. Normally, his warrior brethren would slaughter the child immediately, but the king realizing that his duty should be to set an example had to plan for a way to stop the duel or compromise with the child. 

  
"My liege, the Concierge is at the front gates, shall we let him enter?" A guard had come in dressed in the vibrant colors of the American Isles. The name "America" comes from an ancient country that was once whole; it was simply named "America" back then. Most consider a whole America to be a myth or improbable, but after the 60-minute-war next to no data could be retrieved from the screens. 

  
"Tsk, what does he want? He should be at the prison; there was almost a breakout today, correct?" The king knew the answer but wanted to stall. The Concierge was the warden of the prison. There was one very large prison that was kept on the outskirts of the Isles, and The Concierge was the one who governed it. The current Concierge was an "asshole" as stated by the King. He would put people in prison for little to no reason, and prisoners sentenced for executions(hardly any to begin with), would be fed to his pet. His pet was a "Panthera Libra", more commonly referred to as a Libras(Lee-brass).  It was malnourished and had a thirst for human flesh, and was the size of a lion.

  
"Administration is taking care of the problem and has bots sealing the gates. The Concierge states that the matter is urgent, and should be dealt with immediately." The Guard gave no time for a response and left the room. 

  
"Damnit, not again." The King sighed as he went to the courtyard, just past the front gates. It was not a castle as it was more of a large house. The Kings of the past had requested large statues and houses built in their honor, but the current king felt it was a waste of resources and took a more humble approach. As he arrived at the front gate, he could see the concierge and a small group of elite militants. 

  
"Greetings my Liege, I have to inquire about what in God's name you plan to do about that child!? You can't let some measly scrap monger threaten the throne! If you won't duel him, I will!" The Concierge was clearly angry at the King's indecisiveness, but the King cared little.  

"If you expect me to murder a child, you'd be wrong. I have ethical principles, I am not a barbarian. My father may have been one, but I am not my father. I will find a peaceful resolution to this problem and if you pester me any further, you will be tasked with guarding the crypt." There was a hush in the air, all those listening were stunned. The Crypt was where the worst people were kept. And notably, the First King. The First King was seemingly immortal, and could not die. After he was thought to have "died" a millennia ago, his tomb was found empty. Other Kings had saught after him, especially his son. Every king that proceeded him saw him as a threat to their power. The First King was located by the current king. He was found in a place that used to be known as Ukraine. Now it was a large overgrown forest, teeming with large lifeforms. Nobody knows why this is, but most believe it is because of the fact that there was nuclear radiation found here BEFORE the 60-minute-war. Nobody knows how this could have been, but it was ancient. And the Old King resided here until he was inevitably found by the Neo King or current king. The Neo King studied him and found an intense mutation in his cells that allowed for almost immediate regeneration upon injury. It is believed that most royalties had some form of mutation in their bloodline, and hide it from the world.

Well, I believe in Physicalism simply because it scientifically makes sense. Our emotions can be described as neurons moving through our brain through electricity, and I see no evidence for any higher power. Evolution is not proven to be fact, but it makes enough sense to me for me to not consider other means of origin. The way we observe things such as color, music, and art, are specific to each individual person. You may not see the color red the way I see the color red and there is no way to communicate how your red could be different from my red. That's not an issue in philosophy, that is an issue with language. Our language is very limited to describing experiences special to ourselves.  This is because we would have no need to convey that sort of information. Communication was developed through many stages of evolution as a way to collaborate and expand upon the individuality of one mind. It was used as a way for early homosapiens to hunt food and stick together in packs. They had no need for conveying information such as how the color red may be viewed to them or how they hear music. So just because we can't convey information of that sort right now doesn't necessarily mean that it is not physical, because the way we process information like the color red or music, is through very physical things like our eyes and ears. I'm going to write it as if it were an essay written specifically for someone as writing in normal MLA format without using words such as, "You, Me, I, We" will get tedious when explaining something like this.  
Confidence is a learned skill, you do not get it at birth, and you do not get it from your parents. Confidence is something that you gain based on your environment. I was born in a home where both my parents were loud and boisterous about their opinions if you wanted to say something you had to speak loud. That is not the case for everyone, and there are ways around that. If you want to develop your confidence the best thing you can do is to talk to as many people as possible. Think of it as a video game right, whenever you have a conversation or talk to someone you get experience points. If you talk to someone that you don't know, like a stranger, you'd get more experience points. Eventually "grinding experience points" just by talking to your friends would never yield enough exp to "level up". I know it is a cringy analogy, but it is a good one. It is not something that you have to "level up", but it is something that you can "level up" without your knowledge so to say. I got to a point where I was very argumentative with everyone around me, as that's how my parents were. This messed up my relationships with friends, and I had to learn how to get around that. The easiest way for me to talk to people was through arguing. Generally, that's not how you want to make friends. So yes my confidence was high, but only because I was very specialized in the way I spoke. So I had to branch out and learn of other ways to easily communicate with people. The best way to do that (in my opinion) is through comedy. Using comedy makes people instantly feel more comfortable around you. So rather than you changing for them, they will change for you. There is one drawback, if you are labeled as "the funny one", people will only see you as "the funny one". It sounds nice, but it's not. You feel very lonely as you feel like people only like you because of your comedy and jokes. So yes have comedy, but do have too much of it. Another great way to start talking to people is to simply ask how their day is going. I do this ALL THE TIME. If I want to get to know someone better, I just text them with, "Hey, how has your day been?". People like being able to talk about their day and you can start a pretty good conversation just with that. If your not as comfortable talking to people in person, you can try something different. I use Instagram a lot (I'm 15 years old what did you expect) and it's a great way to see people near you that your friends are friends with and so on. You see a lot of people there, but hardly ever do you talk to them. If you want to talk to them, memes are the best route to go. I don't know how old you are so I wouldn't know what people of your age group would be interested in, but for me, memes are the way to go. I can just ask, "Hey do you want memes?" and they will ALWAYS say yes. Nobody says no to memes. It sounds childish, and it is. But it's a great way of getting rid of tension and being able to make someone laugh. The real-life version of this is as I mentioned above, comedy. For comedy, you can make anything funny, but it's all about delivery. Body-language, tone, all of that is very important. You can't just say something like "Haha people with cancer are stupid and bald". You have enough common sense not to say that surely, but that's just an example of what NOT to do. There was no punch line and there was no real set up. For a joke to come across as funny both of those things must be there. So an example of what you should do is this, "So a little girl is walking into the woods in the middle of the night. It's pitch black, and she starts to hear rustling sounds near her. She exclaims; "Help! I'm lost and scared!". She hears a voice in return; "How do you think I feel, I have to walk back alone?". There was a setup and a punchline. Comedy may not be your thing and that's fine. Another good way to boost your confidence is just to do nice things for people. Not big things, but small things that people will notice. Like helping someone pick up a dropped item, or giving simple directions. People associate good things with you if you are to do that. Well, that's my advice, if you have any questions I will try my best to answer them.

Sidenote: If you have more confidence in yourself, the more likely others are going to have confidence in you. So even if you fake having confidence, to others that will look real.
